classification.difficultyReason: Explicit parts guide the equilibrium check, separation, standard trigonometric integration and substitution of the initial condition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the constant solution of the DE is not a solution of the IVP.

answer.short: The constant solution is $y=1$, which gives $y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=1\ne3$.
answer.worked:
For a constant solution, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$. Set the dependent-variable factor equal to zero:
$$\begin{align*}y-1&=0\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
This gives $y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=1\ne3$, so it is not a solution of the IVP.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use separation of variables to find the general solution of the DE.

answer.short: $y=1+C\sec x$, where $C$ is an arbitrary real constant and $\cos x\ne0$.
answer.worked:
For $y\ne1$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac1{y-1}\,dy&=\tan x\,dx\\\int\frac1{y-1}\,dy&=\int\tan x\,dx\\\ln|y-1|&=-\ln|\cos x|+C_1\\\ln|y-1|&=\ln|\sec x|+C_1\\y-1&=A\sec x\\y&=1+C\sec x\end{align*}$$
Allowing $C=0$ includes the constant solution. The DE requires $\cos x\ne0$.

Substitute $x=\dfrac\pi4$, $y=3$:
$$\begin{align*}3-1&=C\sec\left(\frac\pi4\right)\\2&=C\sqrt2\\C&=\sqrt2\\y&=1+\sqrt2\sec x\end{align*}$$
The interval containing the initial point is $-\dfrac\pi2<x<\dfrac\pi2$.
